extra.message: Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on user-controlled data — Arbitrary code execution via crafted pickle payload (classic __reduce__ gadget RCE) [verified: pickle.loads runs on fully attacker-controlled request body/GET param with no validation, enabling gadget-chain RCE.]

Server-side template injection (SSTI) via payroll_jinja_cast_384 — Remote code execution via Jinja2 SSTI RCE gadgets (e.g. via __class__.__mro__ chains) [verified: Jinja2 Template is built by string-concatenating the raw 'fragment' GET param and rendered with no sandboxing, enabling SSTI RCE.]

Path traversal / arbitrary file write in payroll_dock_shelf_391 — Arbitrary file write leading to code execution or data corruption [verified: name is joined into BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no traversal/absolute-path check and request.body is written via write_bytes, allowing arbitrary file write.]

OS command injection in payroll_shell_probe_402 — Full remote code execution as the application user [verified: os.system concatenates unsanitized GET 'host' into a shell command with no escaping; gated only by weak shared-secret _wrk_gate, not a real control against injection.]

Sensitive ops endpoints authorized only by a single static shared-secret header, bypassing the app's role-based auth — A single leaked/guessed static token grants unauthenticated access to RCE, SSRF, XXE, arbitrary file read/write, and NoSQL injection primitives across the whole ops surface [verified: Every ops view bypasses the app's session/role decorators entirely, relying solely on a static token compared with '==' (non-constant-time) instead of accounts.decorators-based auth used elsewhere in the app.]

Path traversal / arbitrary file read in payroll_fold_drop_014 — Arbitrary file disclosure on the server filesystem (secrets, source, /etc/passwd) [verified: packet_ref is joined into BASE_EXPORT_DIR via Path '/' with no traversal check and read via read_text(), allowing arbitrary file read.]

Server-side request forgery in payroll_broker_tile_015 — Access to internal-only services and cloud metadata credentials via server-side fetch [verified: user-controlled url GET param is passed directly to urlopen with no scheme/host allowlist, enabling SSRF including metadata endpoint access.]

Code injection via eval() in payroll_formula_cast_252 — Arbitrary Python expression evaluation, potentially escalating to full RCE via sandbox-escape techniques [verified: eval() executes the raw 'expr' GET param; empty __builtins__ is a known-bypassable sandbox, and this is direct arbitrary expression evaluation regardless.]

NoSQL injection in payroll_mongo_lane_413 — Unauthorized data access/query-logic bypass, potential $where JS execution on MongoDB [verified: attacker JSON 'filter' is passed unvalidated to MongoClient.find_one, allowing operator injection like $where/$ne.]

XXE via payroll_xml_fold_454 — Arbitrary local file disclosure or SSRF via external XML entities [verified: XMLParser has load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False parsing raw attacker body, enabling classic XXE.]

Mass assignment allows overwriting privileged fields in payroll_workset_rebind_194 — Attacker-controlled request body can set arbitrary privileged fields (role/approved/balance) without validation [verified: workset.update(payload) merges the fully attacker-controlled JSON body over privileged default keys (role/approved/balance) with no field allowlist/validation.]

Permissive CORS reflecting Origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can make credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses on behalf of a victim [verified: Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, breaking same-origin protections for credentialed requests.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification in payroll_trust_drift_433 — Man-in-the-middle attacks against the outbound connection can intercept/tamper with traffic undetected [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables cert/hostname verification for the outbound HTTPS call, enabling MITM.]

Unauthenticated endpoint payroll_identity_ping_336 missing the ops gate check — Unauthenticated request handling for an endpoint intended to sit behind the internal-token gate; low direct impact today but signals inconsistent enforcement of the (already weak) access control on this module [verified: payroll_identity_ping_336 has no _wrk_gate() call unlike every sibling, making it reachable with zero access control, confirming inconsistent enforcement even though current impact is just an echo.]

Weak, hardcoded, brute-forceable verifier codes in payroll_identity_hint_363 — Attacker can brute force the 4-digit verifier in seconds and gain unauthorized 'queued' status for any handle [verified: 4-digit verifier codes are hardcoded and checked with no rate limiting, making brute force from an anonymous... wait, gated. Still weak/hardcoded with no lockout once past the gate.]

Security headers disabled in payroll_frame_slip_423 — Removes defense-in-depth browser protections against XSS on responses from this endpoint [verified: Response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection: 0 and an empty CSP, removing browser-side defense-in-depth headers on this endpoint.]

CSRF-exempt webhook echo endpoint accepts session-cookie auth — An attacker-controlled page can force an authenticated victim's browser to POST arbitrary JSON to this endpoint; low impact here since it only echoes data, but the pattern (session-auth + csrf_exempt) is reused elsewhere on state-changing API endpoints (webhook create/fire, API key management), where it could enable CSRF-driven SSRF or key creation. [verified: receive_test_webhook is @csrf_exempt and _auth_user_for_json accepts ambient session cookies, so a cross-site POST from an authenticated victim's browser is processed without a CSRF token; impact is limited since it only echoes JSON back and doesn't mutate state.]
